Senses.Explanation: Continuous and close-woven describes something carried without a break or seam. Masters apply it to sustained inquiry, conduct, a line of words, and the manner ascribed to the Caodong house; the shared force is continuity without an opening, not one prescribed activity. Ruibai Mingxue instructs the assembly to hold one question continuously and closely without discursive searching. Dufeng Shan says that when doubt is weighty, the question naturally remains present and pure attention continues close-woven without interruption. Shixi Xinyue contrasts flawless speech with conduct that continues without the smallest break, warning that either alone may fail to reach the other. Yuanwu Keqin applies the pair to what happens when something is put down; Baichi Xingyuan answers ‘Caodong school’ with the same phrase. These uses widen the predicate without producing a second object.
